_comment: English overlay for stages.json. Same structure; an empty string means 'use the Korean text'. Keep list lengths equal to stages.json.

stages.label: Scan
stages.title: Band scan
stages.question: Which base stations are around?
stages.intro: Looks at each allowed frequency position in turn and checks whether a base station is sending a synchronisation signal there.
stages.analogy: Like turning a radio dial to find the channels that are on air.

summary.ok_easy: Found {count} base station(s). The strongest is at {freq_mhz} MHz.
summary.ok_expert: {count} cell(s), strongest GSCN {gscn} ({freq_mhz} MHz), PCI {pci}, peak/noise {pnr} dB
summary.fail_easy: No base station signal was found in this band.
summary.fail_expert: PSS correlation peak below threshold ({threshold} dB) on all {n_candidates} candidates

progress.scan.candidate: Checking each position where an SSB could be

gscn.title: From GSCN to the SSB frequency

spectrum.title: Signal strength by frequency
spectrum.caption: Base station signals are where the curve rises. Vertical lines mark the positions an SSB may occupy (GSCN).

cells.title: Base stations found
cells.caption: Pick the base station to follow.

NO_CELL.message: The signal may be too weak to see.
NO_CELL.fix: Raise the receive gain and scan again.

NO_CELL.message: The capture may have been too short and missed the SSB.
NO_CELL.fix: SSBs usually come every 20 ms. Try receiving for longer.

action.label: Retry with double the capture time

NO_CELL.message: There may be no base station in this band, or the antenna may not suit it.
NO_CELL.fix: Check the antenna connection and the band, or pick another band.

NO_CANDIDATE.message: There is no position inside the received band where an SSB could sit.
NO_CANDIDATE.fix: Change the centre frequency or sample rate to widen the band.

CAPTURE_TOO_SHORT.message: The received signal is too short.
CAPTURE_TOO_SHORT.fix: At least 40 ms is needed so that no SSB is missed.

action.label: Retry with double the capture time

RSSI_ONLY_DEVICE.message: This device's bandwidth is too narrow; only the spectrum view is supported.
RSSI_ONLY_DEVICE.fix: Decoding an SSB needs an SDR with more bandwidth.

stages.locked_reason: Scan first to find a base station to follow.
stages.label: SSB
stages.title: SSB sync
stages.question: Getting in step with the base station
stages.intro: Aligns time and frequency to the 'here I am' signal (SSB) that the base station sends at regular intervals.
stages.analogy: Finding a lighthouse and setting your watch to its flashes.

summary.ok_easy: Found the base station's beacon (SSB) and got in step with it.
summary.ok_expert: PCI {pci}, SSB #{ssb_index}, timing {timing_us} µs, CFO {cfo_hz} Hz ({cfo_ppm} ppm), SINR {sinr} dB

progress.ssb.fine_cfo: Measuring and correcting the frequency offset
progress.ssb.pbch: Unfolding the SSB into a grid and checking which SSB it is

rsrp.label: Signal strength (SS-RSRP)
rsrp.note: Shown relative to full scale (dBFS), not as absolute power (dBm), because there is no device calibration.

cfo_total.title: Adding the coarse and fine estimates

ssb_index.title: Reading the SSB index from the DM-RS

correlation.title: PSS correlation
correlation.caption: The sharp peak is the moment the SSB starts. Only the matching one of the three PSS sequences rises high.

ssb_grid.title: SSB resource grid
ssb_grid.caption: Darker cells are stronger. An SSB is 240 subcarriers × 4 symbols.

constellation.title: PBCH constellation
constellation.caption: The more clearly the points gather into four clusters, the easier the notice is to read.

annotations.PSS: Primary sync signal. Aligns time and gives N_ID2.
annotations.SSS: Secondary sync signal. Gives N_ID1 and so fixes the cell ID.
annotations.PBCH: The channel that carries the basic notice (MIB).
annotations.PBCH DM-RS: Reference signal for reading the PBCH. It also tells the SSB index.

NO_SSB.message: The signal may be so weak that the sync signal is buried in noise.
NO_SSB.fix: Raise the receive gain or move the antenna.

NO_SSB.message: The frequency offset may be larger than the search range (satellites, devices with a poor clock).

action.label: Retry with double the search range

NO_SSB.message: There may be no base station on the chosen frequency.
NO_SSB.fix: Go back to the scan and pick another base station.

LOW_SNR.message: Synchronised, but the signal quality is low. Reading may fail in the next step.
LOW_SNR.fix: Raise the gain or move the antenna.

RSRP_UNCALIBRATED.message: Signal strength is an uncalibrated value (dBFS).
RSRP_UNCALIBRATED.fix: If you need absolute power (dBm), enter the device calibration in Settings.

WIDE_CFO_SEARCH.message: This is a satellite (NTN) band, so the CFO search range was widened to allow for Doppler.
WIDE_CFO_SEARCH.fix: The search range can be changed in Settings.

DMRS_AMBIGUOUS.message: The decision on which SSB this is was a close call. The SSB index may be wrong.
DMRS_AMBIGUOUS.fix: Improve the signal quality and synchronise again.

stages.label: MIB
stages.title: MIB
stages.question: Reading the basic notice board
stages.intro: Reads the most basic notice (MIB) carried in the SSB: which frame we are in and where to get the detailed notice (SIB1).
stages.analogy: Reading the sign on a shop door: is it open, and where do I get more information?

summary.ok_easy: Read the base station's basic notice board (MIB).
summary.ok_expert: PBCH CRC OK, SFN={sfn}, half frame={hrf}, k_SSB={k_ssb}, CORESET0 idx={coreset0}, SS0 idx={ss0}
summary.fail_easy: Could not read the notice board (MIB).

monitor_slot.label: Slots to look for the SIB1 pointer

k_ssb.title: k_SSB and whether SIB1 is present

payload.title: What the MIB says
payload.caption: The 24-bit notice split into its fields.

frame.title: Where the SSB sits in the frame
frame.caption: The frame start is worked out backwards from the SSB index and the placement rule (Case).

PBCH_CRC_FAIL.message: Low signal quality corrupted the notice.
PBCH_CRC_FAIL.fix: Raise the gain or move the antenna, then start again from SSB sync.

action.label: Redo from SSB with gain +10 dB

PBCH_CRC_FAIL.message: The synchronisation may be slightly off.
PBCH_CRC_FAIL.fix: Run SSB sync again to realign time and frequency.

PBCH_CRC_FAIL.message: The signal may overlap with another base station's.
PBCH_CRC_FAIL.fix: Go back to the scan and pick another base station.

NO_SIB1_HERE.message: This SSB has no SIB1 pointer attached.
NO_SIB1_HERE.fix: The k_SSB value says 'look on another frequency'. Pick another SSB in the scan.

CELL_BARRED.message: This base station currently bars devices from accessing it (cellBarred).
CELL_BARRED.fix: Reading the broadcast information is not affected.

DEVICE_BW_TOO_NARROW.message: SIB1 is hard to receive with this device: CORESET0 is wider than the device's maximum sample rate.
DEVICE_BW_TOO_NARROW.fix: Use an SDR with more bandwidth, or continue with a stored file.

stages.locked_reason: The MIB tells us where SIB1 is; read it first.
stages.label: SIB1
stages.title: SIB1
stages.question: Reading the access guide
stages.intro: Receives and interprets the detailed notice (SIB1) at the place the MIB pointed to: which network this is and which further notices are broadcast when.
stages.analogy: Picking up a leaflet at the information desk.

summary.ok_easy: This base station belongs to network {plmn}. It broadcasts {si_count} further notice(s).
summary.ok_expert: DCI 1_0 @AL{al}, RIV={riv} → RB {rb_start}+{rb_len}, MCS {mcs}, TBS {tbs} bit, CRC OK

progress.sib1.read: Reading the part that carries SIB1
progress.sib1.pdcch: Looking for the control signal (PDCCH) that points to SIB1

si_window.title: Start of the SI window that carries SIB19

coreset_grid.title: Where SIB1 sits
coreset_grid.caption: CORESET0 in the first symbols carries the control signal saying 'look there'; the SIB1 body follows.

constellation.title: PDSCH constellation
constellation.caption: The signal points of the SIB1 body.

si_schedule.title: Schedule of further notices
si_schedule.caption: Which SIBs are broadcast, and how often.

annotations.CORESET0: The region that carries the control signal pointing to SIB1.
annotations.PDCCH: The control signal that was found.
annotations.PDSCH: The region that carries the SIB1 body.
annotations.PDSCH DM-RS: Reference signal for reading the body.

NO_PDCCH.message: The received band may not cover all of CORESET0.
NO_PDCCH.fix: Raise the sample rate to receive a wider band.

NO_PDCCH.message: Low signal quality may have hidden the control signal.
NO_PDCCH.fix: Raise the gain or move the antenna.

NO_PDCCH.message: The frame timing may be off.

PDSCH_CRC_FAIL.message: The control signal was found but the body has errors.
PDSCH_CRC_FAIL.fix: Raise the gain, or receive longer and try the next transmission.

ASN1_FAIL.message: The body was received but its contents could not be interpreted.
ASN1_FAIL.fix: Check the received bytes in the expert view. The standard release may not match.

NO_SIB19.message: This base station does not broadcast SIB19. It appears to be a terrestrial base station, not a satellite.
NO_SIB19.fix: Pick a base station in a satellite band (n255, n256) to go on to the next step.

stages.locked_reason: SIB1's schedule tells us when SIB19 is broadcast; read it first.
stages.label: SIB19
stages.title: SIB19
stages.question: Reading the satellite guide
stages.intro: Receives SIB19, which only satellite (NTN) base stations broadcast: where the satellite is, which way it moves, and how much delay to compensate.
stages.analogy: A note from a moving satellite saying 'I am here now and heading this way'.

summary.ok_easy: Read the satellite base station's guide (SIB19). The satellite is about {altitude_km} km up, moving at {speed_kms} km/s.
summary.ok_expert: {windows} SI window(s) checked, received {sibs}, epochTime SFN {epoch_sfn}/sf {epoch_sf}, K_offset {k_offset}, ta-Common {ta_common}

progress.si.window: Working out the time window in which SIB19 is broadcast
progress.si.read: Reading that part of the signal

ta_drift_variant.label: Rate of change of the common TA rate

si_windows.title: Time windows in which SIB19 was awaited
si_windows.caption: SIB19 was found inside the window computed from SIB1's schedule.

fields.title: What SIB19 says
fields.caption: Raw values and the physical quantities in the standard's units.

NOT_SCHEDULED.message: This base station does not broadcast SIB19. It appears to be a terrestrial base station, not a satellite.
NOT_SCHEDULED.fix: Scan again in a satellite band (n255, n256).

SI_TIMEOUT.message: The captured span does not contain SIB19's window.
SI_TIMEOUT.fix: Receive for at least one SI period.

action.label: Retry receiving for one SI period

SI_TIMEOUT.message: The satellite may have moved on and the signal weakened.

PDSCH_CRC_FAIL.message: The control signal was found but the body has errors.
PDSCH_CRC_FAIL.fix: Try the transmission in the next period.

ASN1_FAIL.message: The body was received but its contents could not be interpreted.
ASN1_FAIL.fix: Check the received bytes in the expert view.

views.label: NTN
views.title: Satellite calculations
views.question: Where is the satellite, and how late does the signal arrive?
views.intro: Uses the satellite position in SIB19 and your location to work out distance, delay and Doppler.
views.analogy: Just as thunder arrives after the lightning, a satellite's signal arrives late by the distance. That delay is calculated and compensated in advance.
views.locked_reason: SIB19 gives the satellite position; read it first.

summary.ok_easy: The satellite is {elevation}° above the horizon and the signal takes {delay_ms} ms to arrive.
summary.ok_expert: d={range_km} km, el={elevation}°, az={azimuth}°, T_TA={ta_ms} ms, Doppler predicted {doppler} Hz / measured {cfo} Hz (residual {residual} Hz)
summary.fail_easy: The satellite calculations cannot be done.

dt.title: Difference between the reference time (epochTime) and now

propagate.title: Moving the satellite position to the present

sky.title: Sky map
sky.caption: The centre is overhead, the outer circle is the horizon. The line is the satellite's path during the validity time.

delays.title: What the delay is made of
delays.caption: The time (one way) the signal takes from the device via the satellite to the reference point.

ta_curve.title: TA forecast
ta_curve.caption: How the TA will change over the validity time ahead.

doppler_curve.title: Doppler forecast
doppler_curve.caption: The dot is the CFO measured now. Far from the line means an anomaly.

NO_EPHEMERIS.message: SIB19 has no satellite position, or it is in a format that is not supported.
NO_EPHEMERIS.fix: Check ephemerisInfo in the expert view of the SIB19 step.

DOPPLER_MISMATCH.message: The Doppler predicted from the orbit differs a lot from the measured frequency offset.
DOPPLER_MISMATCH.fix: Check that your location setting is right. If it is, the broadcast orbit may differ from the real satellite. Receiver clock error can also cause this.

ORBIT_UNPHYSICAL.message: The broadcast orbit has an altitude or speed that is physically impossible.
ORBIT_UNPHYSICAL.fix: Compare with the circular-orbit speed at this altitude. The values may have been tampered with or broadcast wrongly.

EPOCH_OUT_OF_RANGE.message: The reference time of the satellite information is outside its validity time.
EPOCH_OUT_OF_RANGE.fix: Receive SIB19 again to refresh the values.

EPOCH_IN_FUTURE.message: The reference time is slightly ahead of now. The standard allows this; it is normal.

TA_COMMON_IMPLAUSIBLE.message: The common TA is outside the range of delays possible for a satellite at this altitude.
TA_COMMON_IMPLAUSIBLE.fix: Compare ta-Common with the orbit altitude.

K_OFFSET_TOO_SMALL.message: cellSpecificKoffset is smaller than the calculated TA.
K_OFFSET_TOO_SMALL.fix: A device could not transmit in time with this value. The broadcast value may be wrong.

BELOW_HORIZON.message: The calculation puts the satellite below the horizon. No signal should be receivable from this location.
BELOW_HORIZON.fix: Check that your location setting is right. If it is, the broadcast orbit differs from reality.

SIB19_JUMP.message: Between consecutive SIB19s a value jumped in a way orbital motion does not explain.
SIB19_JUMP.fix: Check the change history on the Tracking screen.

LOCATION_DEFAULT.message: Your location is still the default.
LOCATION_DEFAULT.fix: Enter your real location in Settings for accurate results.

views.label: Track
views.title: Tracking
views.question: What changes over time?
views.intro: Re-reads the same base station at a fixed interval and records how the values change.

REPLAY_NOTE.message: A stored signal is being re-read, so the measurements are the same every time. Only the values calculated from the orbit change with time.
REPLAY_NOTE.fix: Receive live with a device to see real changes.

text.footer: Report produced by nrtrail, a receive-only tool. Values are the broadcast information received and what was calculated from it.

views.label: RA
views.title: Random access observation
views.question: How does the base station answer an access attempt?
views.intro: Reads the base station's response (RAR) to an access attempt and the contention resolution message, from a testbed recording or a synthetic practice signal.
views.analogy: A note answering whoever knocked: 'guest number so-and-so, please speak this much earlier'.
views.locked_reason: SIB1's RACH configuration is needed to find the response.
views.not_allowed: This feature is for testbeds only. It works on synthetic practice signals and on files marked as testbed recordings, and stays closed for live device input.

summary.ok_easy: Read the base station's response (RAR). It told the device to transmit {ta_us} µs earlier.
summary.ok_expert: RA-RNTI {ra_rnti}, RAPID {rapid}, T_A {ta} → N_TA {n_ta} Tc ({distance_m} m), TC-RNTI {tc_rnti}, Msg4 {msg4}

progress.ra.read: Reading the span where the response would be
progress.ra.pdcch: Looking for the control signal announcing the response

groups.rnti: The number used to find the response

msg4_rrc.label: RRC message that came with it

coreset_grid.title: Where the response sits
coreset_grid.caption: Positions of the control signal and the response body.

annotations.CORESET0: The region that carries the control signal.
annotations.PDCCH: The control signal that was found.
annotations.PDSCH: The region that carries the response body.
annotations.PDSCH DM-RS: Reference signal for reading the body.

NO_RAR.message: There is no access response in this span.
NO_RAR.fix: Check that the recording covers an access attempt. The response only appears within ra-ResponseWindow after the preamble.

NO_RAR.message: The RA-RNTI may be different (another PRACH occasion).
NO_RAR.fix: Check that s_id, t_id and f_id in the expert view match the occasion the preamble was actually sent in.

NO_MSG4.message: The response (RAR) was read, but there is no contention resolution message (Msg4) in this span.
NO_MSG4.fix: A longer recording may be needed.

NO_PRACH_CONFIG.message: SIB1 has no RACH configuration, so the number for finding the response cannot be calculated.
NO_PRACH_CONFIG.fix: Check the RACH settings card in the SIB1 step.

UPLINK_NOT_OBSERVED.message: The uplink (preamble, Msg3) is not observed. Only downlink responses are read.
UPLINK_NOT_OBSERVED.fix: Uplink detection is defined as an interface only.

INTERNAL.message: An unexpected error occurred during processing.
INTERNAL.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, check the environment check on the Settings screen and the error text in the expert view.

ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE.message: The engine (MATLAB) needed for this input is not available.
ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE.fix: Check the MATLAB status on the Settings screen. Practice mode works without MATLAB.

CAPTURE_FAILED.message: No signal was received from the device.
CAPTURE_FAILED.fix: Check the device connection and settings (frequency, sample rate).

NO_OCCASION.message: The received span does not contain a moment at which this notice is broadcast.
NO_OCCASION.fix: Receive for at least one broadcast period. For a stored file, a longer recording is needed.

UNSUPPORTED_SEARCH_SPACE.message: This base station points to the notice in a way that is not supported yet (a control region other than CORESET0).
UNSUPPORTED_SEARCH_SPACE.fix: Check the search space settings under pdcch-ConfigCommon in the SIB1 tree (expert view).
